transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles at Kiev
overnight.
Yesterday, Ukraine hit Russia's former imperial capital, St. Petersburg, with about 1,000 drones.
It is Russia that launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, but NPR's Charles Mainz reports
President Trump is demanding that Ukraine stop hitting Russian energy sites.
Trump seems to be trying to protect Russian oil facilities.
Following a deal he cut with President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel, a move Trump
hopes will bring down the price of gas for U.S. voters ahead of midterm elections.
So in that sense, the news of Ukraine striking energy facilities in St. Petersburg Sunday
is unlikely to please Trump, who's already called previous strikes, including one against
Moscow last week, a disgrace.
And here's Charles Mainz in Moscow.
President Trump will fly to Wichita, Kansas today to campaign for incumbent Republican
Senator Roger Marshall.
He's in a close contest for the seat with Democrat Adam Hamilton.
Trump is vowed to campaign steadily to the midterms.
Time is running out for registering to vote for the midterms in some states.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has this rundown of the latest upcoming deadlines.
The window closes today for eligible voters to register or update their registration in
Alabama, Pennsylvania, and South Dakota.
And there's less than a week left until the next major voter registration deadline on
Saturday at some Massachusetts and New York.
Before you know it, it will be Halloween on October 31, which is also the last day in
North Carolina for signing up in person at the state's early voting sites.
If you're already registered, election officials recommend going to your state's official election
website to confirm your status and contact information before the deadline.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their name,
or haven't voted in a while.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
Canadian military officials say a fire killed four Canadian soldiers and badly wounded another
39 this weekend.
This happened during a fire-related training incident at a base in the province of Alberta.
Dan Karpenchuk has more.
Major General L.W. Rutland says officials at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright were aware
of a grass fire for several hours before it quickly spread to the training area where
training activities were underway.
He says the fire was about three-quarters of a mile from the troops, but because of what
he described as uncommonly strong winds, it reached the exercise area in less than a minute.
The Defense Department says there are no indications that this was a terrorist attack.
Rutland says there will be a board of inquiry, but because of the number of casualties and
complexities it could take some time.
Prime Minister Mark Carney says the nation is in mourning after what he called one of
the worst tragedies for the Canadian military in peacetime.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpenchuk in Toronto.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Police in Washington D.C. say a National Guard member's been shot and wounded in the leg.
The D.C. police chief says the Guard member was with several other troops when they were
trying to break up a fight among a group of people on a sidewalk last night.
The chief says a suspect shot and injured the Guard member, and other Guard members
opened fire, wounding the suspect.
None of the injuries sustained is life-threatening.
Artificial intelligence has gotten very good at tracking the paths of hurricanes in the
Atlantic but needs work in the Pacific.
When member station WUSF, Jessica Mizaros reports, meteorologists say they don't fully understand
why AI gets it right or wrong.
Google DeepMind's AI model was spot-on about Hurricane Isaias' path in the Gulf, while
missing the mark for Hurricane Simon in the eastern Pacific.
Brian McNoldy, a hurricane researcher at the University of Miami, says, "AI doesn't use
complicated math and science the way conventional prediction models do."
It makes us a little uncomfortable because we like to know why you're getting the right
answer, and I feel like we don't, or at least I don't.
AI creates forecasts based on patterns from thousands of past storms and atmospheric data.
Forecasters say Google DeepMind's projection for storm strength also needs some work.
For NPR News, I'm Jessica Mizaros in Tampa, Florida.
Pope Leo gave his regular Sunday blessing yesterday in public at the Vatican.
It's been less than a week since he was hospitalized for cancer surgery.
He was discharged on Saturday.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Russia and Ukraine trade missile and drone strikes, with Trump urging Ukraine to stop hitting Russian energy sites
Trump to campaign in Wichita, Kansas for Senator Roger Marshall ahead of close midterm race
Voter registration deadlines approaching in Alabama, Pennsylvania, South Dakota, Massachusetts, New York, and North Carolina
Four Canadian soldiers killed and 39 wounded in grass fire during training at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright
National Guard member shot in the leg while breaking up a fight in Washington, D.C.
Google DeepMind AI hurricane forecasts accurate for Isaias but off on Hurricane Simon in Pacific
Pope Leo gives Sunday blessing at Vatican less than a week after cancer surgery discharge
